_comment: Module definition and the source of truth for building the DataSource in a portal. Same layout as lm-tls-cert-expiry's module JSON; not LogicMonitor's export format.
name: Outage_Reporter_Health
description: Technical and business health of the Outage Reporter service (Example Power & Light, fictional), read from its /health endpoint.

alertMessage.subject: Outage Reporter on ##HOST##: ##DATAPOINT## is ##VALUE## (##LEVEL##)
alertMessage.body:
Datapoint ##DATAPOINT## on ##HOST## is ##VALUE##, crossing threshold ##THRESHOLD##.
Check: on the VM, curl -s localhost:8080/health and journalctl -u outage-reporter --since -15min
Resource: ##HOST##   Level: ##LEVEL##

datapoints.name: reachable
datapoints.description: 1 if /health returned an Outage Reporter health document (HTTP 200 or 503), 0 if nothing usable answered. When 0, every other datapoint is NaN.

alertMessage.subject: Outage Reporter is not answering on ##HOST##
alertMessage.body:
The collector could not get a health document from ##HOSTNAME## (/health on outage.port): stopped, crashed, port closed, or hung for 5 s. Customers cannot report outages online.
Check: systemctl status outage-reporter; journalctl -u outage-reporter -n 50
Resource: ##HOST##   Level: ##LEVEL##

datapoints.name: httpStatus
datapoints.description: HTTP status of /health: 200 for UP or DEGRADED, 503 for DOWN.

datapoints.name: responseTimeMs
datapoints.description: How long the /health request took from the collector, in ms.

datapoints.name: status
datapoints.description: Summary: 0 = UP, 1 = DEGRADED, 2 = DOWN. For dashboards; alerts come from the cause datapoints so one fault raises one alert.

datapoints.name: uptimeSeconds
datapoints.description: Seconds since the service started. Drops to near zero on every restart.

datapoints.name: requestRate
datapoints.description: Requests per second (excluding /health), from the requestsTotal counter.

datapoints.name: serverErrorRate
datapoints.description: 5xx responses per second, from the errorsTotal counter.

datapoints.name: clientErrorRate
datapoints.description: 4xx responses per second (bad input, unknown tickets), from the clientErrorsTotal counter.

datapoints.name: p95LatencyMs
datapoints.description: 95th percentile request latency over the service's last 60 s, in ms.

alertMessage.subject: Outage Reporter is slow on ##HOST##: p95 ##VALUE## ms
alertMessage.body:
p95 latency over the last 60 s is ##VALUE## ms, crossing ##THRESHOLD##. Customers reporting outages are waiting on a spinner, and some will give up and call instead.
Check: GC and CPU on the JVM graphs; chaosMode on this DataSource; journalctl -u outage-reporter | grep ms=
Resource: ##HOST##   Level: ##LEVEL##

datapoints.name: errorRatePct
datapoints.description: Share of requests over the last 60 s that returned 5xx, in percent.

alertMessage.subject: Outage Reporter is failing requests on ##HOST##: ##VALUE##% 5xx
alertMessage.body:
##VALUE##% of requests in the last 60 s returned a server error, crossing ##THRESHOLD##. failedReportsLastMinute shows how many customers could not report an outage.
Check: LM Logs for this resource, filter level=ERROR or status=500
Resource: ##HOST##   Level: ##LEVEL##

datapoints.name: storeOk
datapoints.description: 1 if the ticket store can take writes, else 0. 0 makes the service report DOWN (HTTP 503).

alertMessage.subject: Outage Reporter cannot write its store on ##HOST##
alertMessage.body:
The ticket store is not accepting writes: new outage reports are refused, and the dispatcher cannot record confirmations, crews or restorations. Ticket lookups still work.
Check: df -h /var/lib/outage-reporter; ls -l /var/lib/outage-reporter; journalctl -u outage-reporter | grep -E 'store_|dispatcher_'
Resource: ##HOST##   Level: ##LEVEL##

datapoints.name: chaosMode
datapoints.description: Fault injection in effect: 0 = off, 1 = latency, 2 = errors, 3 = store, 4 = storm. Non-zero means an alert was caused on purpose.

datapoints.name: reportsLastMinute
datapoints.description: Customer outage reports accepted in the last 60 s (synthetic checks excluded). The intake rate; storm response is declared at 60.

datapoints.name: failedReportsLastMinute
datapoints.description: Report submissions in the last 60 s that got a 5xx: customers who tried to report an outage and could not. The business face of errorRatePct and storeOk, so no threshold of its own.

datapoints.name: openOutages
datapoints.description: Outage tickets not yet restored.

datapoints.name: customersAffected
datapoints.description: Customers without power across confirmed open outages, capped per service area at the customers it serves.

datapoints.name: awaitingTriage
datapoints.description: Reports not yet confirmed: customers who have reported and have no ETR yet. Normally under 5; it grows only when reports arrive faster than triage capacity (180 a minute by default).

alertMessage.subject: Outage reports are backing up on ##HOST##: ##VALUE## awaiting triage
alertMessage.body:
##VALUE## outage reports are waiting to be confirmed, crossing ##THRESHOLD##. Reports are arriving faster than they can be triaged, so customers are waiting without an estimated restoration time. The service itself is healthy: this is a capacity alert, not a fault.
Act: start storm staffing (more triage capacity); check reportsLastMinute and the service-area view for where the surge is landing.
Resource: ##HOST##   Level: ##LEVEL##

datapoints.name: oldestOpenMinutes
datapoints.description: Age of the oldest open outage ticket, in minutes. Normal restorations take 6–15 minutes in this compressed model, up to about 30 under storm response.

alertMessage.subject: An outage on ##HOST## has been open ##VALUE## minutes
alertMessage.body:
The oldest open outage ticket is ##VALUE## minutes old, crossing ##THRESHOLD##: about twice the longest restoration the model expects, even under storm response. Something has stalled.
Check: overdueOutages; storeOk; journalctl -u outage-reporter | grep dispatcher_
Resource: ##HOST##   Level: ##LEVEL##

datapoints.name: overdueOutages
datapoints.description: Open outages more than 30 s past their estimated restoration time: promises to customers that were missed. Context for storeOk and oldestOpenMinutes, so no threshold of its own.

datapoints.name: stormMode
datapoints.description: 1 while storm response is in effect (60 or more reports in the last minute), else 0. Customers see a storm banner and longer ETRs.
